long_biography.plain_text:
When the Kulczyk family estate was divided in 2018, Dominika Kulczyk took control of Polenergia as her brother prepared to sell the energy business. She instead defended the company from a competing offer and committed inherited capital to a renewable strategy. The decision made her the dominant shareholder of a platform originally assembled by her father, but placed its future direction under her own stewardship.

As supervisory-board chair, Kulczyk has backed Polenergia's shift towards wind and solar generation. The group partnered with Equinor on Baltic offshore projects and later brought in Brookfield as a strategic investor, using outside capital and expertise while retaining family influence. Her role is strategic rather than executive: she sets direction through ownership and board leadership as professional managers run the business.
